TermTranslation.definition: Very bad pain that happens suddenly or gets worse quickly.
An unwanted, bad or harmful response to a drug or other therapy.
The body's immune response to something that enters the body, such as pollen, dust or certain drugs.
A very bad, possibly deadly, allergic reaction.
A person who is still living after being diagnosed with cancer.
Pain that happens slowly, lasts a long time or gets worse over time.
Losing too much water from the body.
Any drug or substance that causes the body to make more urine.
Feeling very tired or not having enough energy.
A build-up of fluid in the body.
Balding or loss of hair from the scalp or body.
The cells and organs that defend the body against infection, disease and other materials that enter the body.
Not being able to have children.
Difficulty falling or staying asleep or not getting enough good sleep.
Feeling sick to the stomach or the need to vomit.
Pain from an injury to or problem with nerves, the spinal cord or the brain.
A record that people with chronic pain keep to track when pain is greatest during the day and the amount of medicine or other treatments that make the pain go away.
Treatment and support to relieve symptoms and improve quality of life for people with a serious illness that cannot be cured.
Pain, numbness, tingling or itching that someone feels where a removed limb used to be.
Inflammation of a vein causing redness, swelling and pain.
Infection of one or both lungs caused by bacteria, viruses or fungi.
Symptoms caused by large doses of radiation.
Describing the strength of pain based on a scale. For example, 1 to 10 where 1 means no pain or very little pain and 10 is the worst pain.
An unwanted, bad or harmful symptom or effect caused by a medical treatment or procedure.
Pain from an injury to or problem with the skin and deep tissues.
Pain in any organ in the chest or belly.
Throwing up the contents of the stomach through the mouth.
